title.narrative: Främja ungdomsarbete genom stöd till TVET
Promoting Youth Employment Through Support to TVET

description.narrative:
Svenska ambassaden i Monrovia har fått en förfrågan från UNIDO för finansiering av USD 6,213,870, uppskattat 55 miljoner kronor för att genomföra Promoting youth employment by supporting technical and vocational education i Liberia för perioden 2018–2023. UNIDO kommer vara huvudansvariga för att implementera projektet.
Projektets övergripande mål är att lyfta unga från fattigdom genom att ge dem ökade möjligheter till en produktiv anställning via ett robust och inkluderande TVET-system (Technical Vocational Education and Training), med kännedom om marknadens ekonomiska behov. Projektet kommer bidra till följande resultat: - ökad kapacitet hos lärare genom formell lärarutbildning som fokuserar på yrkesförberedande utbildning - stärkt kompentens bland befolkningensfärdigheter så att det överensstämmer med de ekonomiska behoven (till exempel infrastrukturutveckling och jordbruk) - öka engagemanget hos privata sektorn för delaktighet inom TVET-sektorn
Utveckling av ungdomar kommer vara i fokus, vilket kommer uppnås genom att stärka och bygga på nuvarande institutionell kapaciteterna hos Liberias tekniska och yrkesförberande utbildnings system för att leverera relevanta kurser som svarar till behoven hos ekonomin.
Projektet kommer adressera både efterfrågan och utbudet på arbetsmarknadens genom att utrusta ungdomar med färdigheter som ökar deras möjlighet till anställning, och som resultat minskar nuvarande hinder för företag att expandera på grund av brist på kompetent arbetskraft.

UNIDO has applied to Sida for funding of USD 6,213,870, aproximately 55 million SEK, to carry out the promoting youth employment by supporting technical and vocational education in Liberia programme during the period 2018-2023. UNIDO will be the main implementing partner.
The proposed intervention overall objective is to lift beneficiaries from poverty by increasing their chances to gain productive employment through a robust and inclusive TVET system (Technical Vocational Education and Training) that is responsive to economic needs. The intervention will support the following outputs: - improved capacity of teachers through participation in formal teacher training for vocational education; - strengthened human capital to correspond to economic needs (e.g. in infrastructure development and agribusiness); - and increased participation of the private-sector in stewardship and engagement with TVET sector at the school level.
Emphasis will be placed on youth development. This will be achieved by strengthening and building on the existing institutional capacity of Liberia's vocational training system to deliver up-to-date training courses relevant to the requirements of the economy.
The intervention will address both labor demand and supply by equipping young persons with skills that increase their employability and earnings, and by removing bottlenecks to expanding profitable businesses due to skills shortages.

The overall objective of the contribution is to lift beneficiaries from poverty by increasing their chances to gain productive employment. The expected outcome is a robust and inclusive Technical and Vocation Education and Training (TVET) system that is responsive to economic needs.

The intervention started in January 2019 and orginally planned to end in 2023. However, there was a ''no cost extension'' in 2023 that extended the program to December 2024 as end of activities period. To achieve program objective of contributing to an inclusive Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) system that is responsive to economic needs, in December 2024, there was an amendment to the program that was signed which extended the current program to December 2026.
Here are some of the keyy results achieved thus far:
Infrastructure Development - Renovation and construction a modern TVET facility equipped with state-of-the-art workshops to enhance hands-on training. Completed 13 out of 13 planned construction/rehabilitation works to upgrade school facilities. Established a Library and Resource Center (2023) with a 40-student capacity and computer space. Integrated practical training by having students design and produce the furniture for the resource center as part of their Masters training class.
Teacher Capacity Building-Strengthening the competencies of TVET instructors through targeted training and professional development programs.
Significant progress was made in strengthening TVET teacher capacity to enhance technical education delivery at Voinjama Multilateral High School (VMHS). Of the twelve (12) required TVET teachers, nine (9) newly recruited instructors are currently undergoing specialized training in various skills abroad. The status of the training is as follows:
Four (4) teachers have completed their training and returned. Five (5) teachers remain in training. Three (3) additional teachers have been recruited and are preparing for training.
Additionally, existing TVET teachers at VMHS continue to receive both technical and pedagogical training to enhance their instructional capabilities. Furthermore, the TVET Center for Professional Training, Research, and Innovation (TCPTRI), based at the Booker Washington Institute (BWI), became fully operational during the year, providing a vital platform for continuous professional development.
The period also recorded the development and adoption of seven Level 4 curricula for five trades at VMHS, with two additional curricula adopted for the electrical trade. Establishment of a Centre for TVET Teacher Certification (TCPTRI), finalized in 2023. Formal TVET Teacher Pedagogical Training launched in May and September 2023, with the first two cohorts including three male participants from VMHS out of 58 total trainees (six female participants).
Private Sector Engagement:
To ensure TVET education aligns with market needs, the program actively engaged industry stakeholders, private sector subject matter experts in the demand-driven curriculum development process. Additionally:
Small business owners were provided with awareness on the technical training potential of VMHS. The program facilitated interactions between the school administration and local businesses, fostering partnerships that strengthen practical training opportunities for students.
Inclusive Education:
Promoting equal access to TVET by implementing measures that support the participation of women, vulnerable youth, and persons with disabilities. Through these efforts, the program is strengthening TVET's role in workforce development, ensuring its relevance, accessibility, and sustainability.
The program continued to promote inclusivity within the TVET sector by implementing several key initiatives:
A first-round inclusive education training was provided to TVET teachers and staff at VMHS, equipping them with skills to better support diverse student needs. The project collaborated with Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) to raise awareness in communities and schools, encouraging greater female participation in TVET, including individuals with disabilities. Awareness campaigns were conducted in partnership with CSOs to address Sexual and Gender-Based Violence (SGBV), ensuring a safer learning environment for all students.
Increased Enrollment
A notable and unexpected impact of the program has been a significant increase in student enrollment at VMHS. Since the programs inception, enrollment has grown by nearly 90%, as students anticipate gaining access to improved TVET opportunities.
Before the project began, VMHS had approximately 920 students enrolled. As of the current reporting period, enrollment has surged to 1,750 studentsa testament to the growing interest in TVET education and the programs impact on student aspirations.
